brief: 6 writing tips for founders who hate writing.

slots.headline: Six Writing Tips for Founders Who Absolutely Hate Writing

slots.title: Talk It Out
slots.body: Record your thoughts as voice notes and let AI transcribe them. Speaking naturally beats staring at a blank page. Edit the transcript into clean copy in minutes.

slots.title: Bullet Your Ideas
slots.body: Start with a messy list of bullet points instead of full sentences. Each bullet is one idea. Rearrange them until they flow, then add transitions.

slots.title: Write to One
slots.body: Picture one specific customer or investor reading your words. Writing for a crowd creates corporate fluff. A single reader forces clarity and tone.

slots.title: Use a Timer
slots.body: Give yourself fifteen minutes and permission to write garbage. A deadline kills perfectionism. You can always edit bad words, but not a blank page.

slots.title: State the Point
slots.body: Decide your one-sentence takeaway before you begin. Knowing the destination keeps you from wandering. Build everything backward from that final line.

slots.title: Separate Drafts
slots.body: Never edit while you write. Turn off the red pen and dump every thought onto the page. Polish comes only after the idea exists.

slots.headline: Make Writing Your Secret Weapon
slots.body: Writing is a muscle, not a talent. Start messy, publish anyway, and watch your clarity compound weekly.
